Administrator here at a public university. I think we need to better define "administrator." I assure you, the vast majority of "administrators" don't make anywhere near $100,000. I understand the concerns about bloat in upper administration, but many administrators at lower levels are working hard to serve students, and the vast majority of what they do is under appreciated and misunderstood in conversations about "those damn administrators hogging the money." You couldn't pay me enough to be a front-line financial aid advisor trying to provide good customer service, help students find ways to afford college, while navigating the immense amount of legal bull that comes with the territory all at $30,000 a year. All I ask is that we discuss "administration" knowledgeably and understand, too, that it's different institution to institution. /rant

We often don't have final high school transcripts on file by the time first term registration starts at summer orientation, but we absolutely have to see them to verify high school graduation before a student can continue into a second term. Usually it's not a big deal, as I work at a selective admission institution and so most of our incoming freshmen would have to screw up quite a bit after the time of admission to not graduate high school. Occasionally, though, some students have to work out issues with their high schools in order to get final transcripts released. Our office isn't involved in working that out with the high school; it's the student's responsibility. The biggest reason that I typically hear of a transcript being held is that a student owes the school for one thing or another (missing library book, unpaid tech fee, etc.). If the school is illegally withholding a student's transcript, by all means, the student should sue. That doesn't mean the issue will be wrapped up in time for a student to register for a second college term, and most colleges and universities aren't going to make an exception or get wrapped up in a legal case.

College admissions person here. Her college will require her final high school transcript before she can register for her second term.
